outline.core_hook: Teams manage multiple gateways and suffer configuration-driven outages — Nexus centralizes gateway control to cut config time and outages while enabling zero-downtime scaling.

slides.slide_title: Nexus API Gateway
slides.subtitle: One gateway. Every API. Zero downtime.
slides.narrative_role: Introduce the product and tagline so the audience understands the single-line value promise that the rest of the deck will prove with problems, mechanics, results and timeline.
key_messages: Nexus API Gateway
One gateway. Every API. Zero downtime.
slides.visual_emphasis: big product name and tagline as hero

slides.label: THE PROBLEM
slides.slide_title: Multiple gateways create time drain and operational risk
slides.subtitle: Observed across engineering organizations
slides.narrative_role: Establishes the operational pain that Nexus must resolve, creating the tension the core_hook names (multiple gateways → outages & blind spots).
key_messages: Teams manage 4+ separate gateways averaging 2.3 hours/week each on config
68% of outages last quarter traced to gateway misconfiguration
No unified view of API traffic across services — teams fly blind
These operational issues increase risk, slow development, and make incidents harder to diagnose.
slides.visual_emphasis: three pain-point bullets as hero with a short impact summary

slides.label: PRODUCT · PIPELINE
slides.slide_title: Five-step pipeline unifies connection, routing, security, monitoring, and scale
slides.subtitle: From existing APIs to zero-downtime scaling
slides.narrative_role: Explains how Nexus resolves the problem by showing the end-to-end mechanics that eliminate fragmented gateways and provide unified control and visibility.
key_messages: Connect → Route → Secure → Monitor → Scale
Connect — point Nexus at your existing APIs via auto-discovery
Route — drag-and-drop routing rules with automatic conflict detection
Secure — one-click mTLS, rate limiting, and OAuth2 per-route
Monitor — unified dashboard with per-route latency, error rates, throughput
Scale — auto-scaling based on traffic patterns with zero-downtime deploys
slides.visual_emphasis: process flow with step descriptions; ordered process as hero

slides.label: BETA RESULTS
slides.slide_title: Private beta delivered large improvements in operations and developer experience
slides.subtitle: Measured during private beta
slides.narrative_role: Deepens the deck's tension by resolving it with measured outcomes from the private beta — demonstrating the platform's ability to cut config time, reduce outages, and improve latency and NPS.
key_messages: Config Time: 15 min/wk (-89%)
Outages: 1/quarter (-92%)
API Latency: 38ms (-73%)
Dev NPS: 71 (+49 pts)
These metrics were observed during our private beta and indicate material improvement in stability and developer satisfaction.
slides.visual_emphasis: KPI tiles as hero with one-line contextual note

slides.label: VALUE PROP
slides.slide_title: Consolidate gateways to reduce risk, save time, and restore visibility
slides.narrative_role: Summarizes why the measured improvements matter for customers and what operational changes Nexus unlocks for engineering teams.
key_messages: Reduces configuration overhead and human error by centralizing route and policy management
Prevents routing conflicts and enforces consistent security per-route to improve reliability
Provides a single source of truth for traffic and performance so teams can diagnose issues faster
Enables safe, zero-downtime autoscaling and deployments so traffic-driven growth doesn't cause outages
slides.visual_emphasis: benefit statements as the primary focus with supporting icons

slides.label: LAUNCH TIMELINE
slides.slide_title: Clear rollout path from private beta to compliance-certified GA
slides.subtitle: Oct 2026 → Apr 2027
slides.narrative_role: Closes the deck by showing the concrete launch milestones and timing that move Nexus from private beta to GA with compliance certifications.
key_messages: Oct 2026: Private beta (12 customers)
Dec 2026: Public beta, self-serve signup
Feb 2027: GA launch + enterprise tier
Apr 2027: SOC2 + HIPAA certification

outline.deck_title: Unlocking the Next Phase of Growth for XTSY on Quick Commerce
outline.core_hook: Quick Commerce is becoming a primary consumption channel for impulse and instant-need beverage categories, but visibility, availability and repeat purchase gaps limit XTSY's scale — data-led commerce execution and automation close the gap.

slides.slide_title: Unlocking the Next Phase of Growth for XTSY on Quick Commerce
slides.subtitle: Building Category Share, Visibility and Consumer Penetration Through Data-Led Commerce Execution
slides.narrative_role: Introduce the central opportunity: quick commerce is a strategic growth channel for XTSY and sets the agenda for the rest of the deck (what to optimize and why).
key_messages: Status: XTSY live on Zepto, Swiggy Instamart and Blinkit
Quick Commerce is becoming a primary consumption channel for impulse and instant-need beverage categories, creating a significant opportunity for XTSY to scale.
slides.visual_emphasis: ecosystem map showing Zepto, Blinkit and Instamart connected to XTSY growth engine (visual hero)

slides.slide_title: Why the Energy Drink Category is Built for Quick Commerce
slides.narrative_role: Establish the behavioural fit between energy-drink consumption occasions and the instant-fulfilment value proposition of quick commerce, creating demand-side justification for investment.
key_messages: Consumer purchase occasions by daypart: Pre-workout consumption; Gaming sessions; Late-night work/study; Travel & commuting; Party & social occasions; Instant energy requirements
Key Insight: Energy drinks have one of the strongest instant-need consumption behaviors, making them highly compatible with Quick Commerce.
Show: Category growth drivers · Consumer demand moments · Impulse purchase behaviour
slides.visual_emphasis: daypart occasions map as hero with demand moments and impulse behavior callouts

slides.slide_title: Growth Opportunities for XTSY Across Quick Commerce Platforms
slides.narrative_role: Translate consumer fit into platform-specific opportunity areas so stakeholders can see where to act across visibility, conversion and retention levers.
key_messages: Opportunity Matrix rows: Visibility · Conversion · Repeat Purchase · Market Expansion
Opportunity Matrix columns: Zepto · Blinkit · Instamart

Opportunity Areas: Search visibility expansion · Sponsored placements · Category page dominance · New city penetration · Portfolio expansion · Basket attachment opportunities · Subscription/repeat purchase growth
Key Takeaway: Growth is not limited to ad spends; it is unlocked through visibility, availability, discoverability and repeat purchase strategies.
slides.visual_emphasis: matrix as hero (rows = levers, columns = platforms) with opportunity bullets per cell

slides.slide_title: Our 4-Phase Framework to Build Category Share
slides.narrative_role: Provide a stepwise roadmap that links foundational fixes to market-share capture and then to scalable, profitable growth — so investments map to outcomes.
key_messages: Phase 1: Foundation & Hygiene · Availability tracking · OOS reduction · Search audit · Visibility benchmark · Portfolio prioritization
Phase 2: Market Share Capture · Search dominance · Sponsored placements · Keyword expansion · Competitor conquesting · Category page visibility
Phase 3: Consumer Expansion · New-to-brand acquisition · New-to-category targeting · Cross-platform expansion · Geo expansion
Phase 4: Scale & Profitability · Automation-led optimization · Incrementality focus · Repeat purchase acceleration · Portfolio scaling
Show progression from Visibility → Offtakes → Market Share → Profitability
slides.visual_emphasis: 4-stage roadmap as hero showing phased progression from foundation to profitability

slides.slide_title: How Our Commerce Intelligence Platform Drives Faster Growth

key_messages: Visual: Control Tower Dashboard (platform control tower as visual)
TRACKING: Share of Search · Share of Shelf · Availability Monitoring · Pricing Intelligence · Competitor Monitoring
INSIGHTS: SKU-level performance · City-level opportunity mapping · Platform-wise growth pockets · Category trends
Key Message: What gets measured gets scaled.

slides.slide_title: Ads Automation Engine Designed for Quick Commerce
slides.narrative_role: Show how automation shortens decision cycles and improves efficiency so advertising and visibility investments convert into faster business outcomes.
key_messages: Automation workflow: Platform Data → Decision Engine → Bid Optimization · Budget Reallocation · Keyword Expansion · Placement Optimization → Business Outcome
Benefits: Faster optimization cycles · Reduced manual intervention · Improved ROAS · Improved share of visibility · Higher conversion efficiency
Highlight: Automation allows brands to react in hours instead of weeks.

slides.slide_title: Expected Business Impact for XTSY
slides.narrative_role: Synthesize how combined intelligence, automation and execution map to business outcomes XTSY cares about (visibility → offtakes → share).

outline.core_hook: CHEFFIN is spending heavily across FLIPCART and ZAROMA but the current traffic economics are structurally weak — CPCs are far above what current AOV and CVR can support, so campaign-level fixes alone won't restore profitability.

slides.slide_title: CHEFFIN FLIPCART & ZAROMA Ads Audit
slides.subtitle: Last 90 Days Performance Review | Key Gaps, Opportunities & Takeover Roadmap
slides.narrative_role: Open the deck with the engagement scope and set expectations for a concise audit that ties performance to operating gaps and a takeover roadmap.
key_messages: Prepared by our agency
Scope: FLIPCART Targeting (last 90 days), FLIPCART Search Term report, ZAROMA April–June campaign, city and keyword views
slides.visual_emphasis: cover with marketplace growth theme and FLIPCART + ZAROMA visual cues

slides.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
slides.slide_title: The account is spending at scale, but not yet buying profitable demand.
slides.narrative_role: Establish the high-level performance picture and introduce the central diagnosis that explains why current spend is not translating to profitable sales.
key_messages: Combined spend: ₹114.9L
Combined revenue: ₹37.4L
Combined ROAS: 0.33x
FLIPCART ROAS: 0.34x
ZAROMA ROAS: 0.32x
Main insight: Both FLIPCART and ZAROMA show the same structural issue: CPC is too high relative to AOV and CVR.
Callout: “This is a media economics problem, not just a campaign hygiene problem.”
slides.visual_emphasis: KPI scorecard (combined + platform ROAS) with one-line insight callout

slides.label: ECONOMICS
slides.slide_title: CPC is nearly 3x higher than what current conversion economics can support.
slides.narrative_role: Deepen the tension by quantifying the gap between actual CPC and the break-even (allowable) CPC derived from current AOV and CVR, showing why bids alone cannot fix profitability.
key_messages: Platform | Actual CPC | Allowable CPC for 1.0x ROAS | Gap
FLIPCART | ₹31.1 | ₹10.7 | Actual CPC is ~2.9x allowable
ZAROMA | ₹46.2 | ₹14.8 | Actual CPC is ~3.1x allowable
Main insight: At the current AOV and CVR, the brand needs CPC reduction, CVR improvement, AOV improvement, or all three together.
slides.visual_emphasis: bar chart comparing actual CPC vs allowable CPC (platform-level)

slides.label: DATA & METHODOLOGY
slides.slide_title: We rebuilt the audit from raw performance data, not surface-level reports.
slides.narrative_role: Show the evidence base and data hygiene steps to establish credibility for the metrics and gaps presented in the audit.
key_messages: Data sources reviewed: FLIPCART Targeting last 90 days report
Data sources reviewed: FLIPCART Search Term report
Data sources reviewed: ZAROMA campaign-level data
Data sources reviewed: ZAROMA city-level data
Data sources reviewed: ZAROMA keyword-level data
Note: Some FLIPCART pivot metrics were unreliable or zeroed, so ratios were recalculated from raw data.
Note: ZAROMA sheets appear to have different coverage; campaign-level totals were used as the primary platform total source and city/keyword sheets were used for diagnostics.
Key formulas: ROAS = Revenue or Sales / Spend
Key formulas: ACOS = Spend / Sales
Key formulas: CTR = Clicks / Impressions
Key formulas: CPC = Spend / Clicks
Key formulas: CVR = Orders or Purchases / Clicks
Key formulas: CPA = Spend / Orders or Purchases
Key formulas: AOV = Sales / Orders or Purchases
Key formulas: Allowable CPC for 1.0x ROAS = AOV × CVR
slides.visual_emphasis: source list with two short data-quality callouts

slides.label: FLIPCART SNAPSHOT
slides.slide_title: FLIPCART is generating traffic, but at weak revenue efficiency.
slides.narrative_role: Present the FLIPCART platform metrics that show volume but poor revenue efficiency, reinforcing the need for structural fixes rather than only tactical changes.
key_messages: Spend: ₹29.4L
Ad sales: ₹10.1L
ROAS: 0.34x
Allowable CPC for 1.0x ROAS: ₹10.7
Main insight: FLIPCART’s CPC is almost 3x higher than the CPC the current AOV and CVR can support.
slides.visual_emphasis: metric scorecard with small supporting table (platform KPIs)

slides.label: FLIPCART DIAGNOSIS
slides.slide_title: SBT and exact match are the strongest pockets; discovery layers are dragging ROAS down.
slides.narrative_role: Diagnose which ad types and match/targeting layers are working and which are not, to justify protecting high-performing pockets and tightening control on discovery/low-intent layers.
key_messages: Ad Type | Spend Share | Sales Share | ROAS | Interpretation
SP: Spend Share 75.6%, Sales Share 75.3%, ROAS 0.34x, Interpretation: Main volume driver, but inefficient overall
SBV: Spend Share 12.8%, Sales Share 8.5%, ROAS 0.23x, Interpretation: Weak video efficiency
SBT: Spend Share 9.3%, Sales Share 15.1%, ROAS 0.56x, Interpretation: Best ad type; under-allocated
SD: Spend Share 2.4%, Sales Share 1.1%, ROAS 0.17x, Interpretation: Weak conversion quality
Match/targeting performance: Exact ROAS: 0.44x; Phrase ROAS: 0.26x; Auto ROAS: 0.30x; Category ROAS: 0.25x; Broad ROAS: 0.22x; Audience ROAS: 0.15x
Main insight: Exact match and SBT should be protected and scaled carefully. Phrase, auto, category, broad, and audience layers need tighter control.
slides.visual_emphasis: two mini-tables: ad-type breakdown (hero) and match-type ROAS (supporting)

slides.subtitle: Where we stand, what is working, and the 90-day plan to scale profitably

Prepared by the Growth Team | October 2026

slides.slide_title: Repeat customers now drive most of BREWLY's revenue.

Revenue growth: +38%
Blended ROAS: 2.4x
Customer acquisition cost: ₹410
62% of revenue comes from repeat customers, up from 41% a year ago.
Quarterly revenue (₹ Cr): Q1 FY26: 2.6 | Q2 FY26: 2.9 | Q3 FY26: 3.3 | Q4 FY26: 3.6 | Q1 FY27: 3.9 | Q2 FY27: 4.4
